comment: This configuration file was automatically created by GParserBuilder
The number of threads used to simultaneously adapt and recombine individuals
0 means "automatic"
The maximum allowed number of iterations
The minimum allowed number of iterations
The maximum allowed number of iterations without improvement
0 means: no constraint.
The name of a file which, when modified after the start of an
optimization run, instructs Geneva to terminate optimitation.
This can be used to "touch a file" after the start of an optimization
run, which will lead to the termination of the run after the current iteration.
Activates (1) or de-activates (0) the "touched termination"
The number of iterations without improvement after which
individuals are asked to update their internal data structures
through the actOnStalls() function. A value of 0 disables this check
Time-to-live (in dispatch rounds) of a networked consumer's late-return
buffer entry. A late return not reaped within this many rounds is evicted.
Capacity of a networked consumer's late-return buffer, as a multiple of
the population size. 0 disables late-return buffering entirely.
The number of iterations after which a report should be issued
Indicates how many "best" individuals should be recorded in each iteration
The number of iterations after which a checkpoint should be written.
-1 means: Write a checkpoint file whenever an improvement was encountered
0 means: Never emit checkpoint files.
The directory where checkpoint files should be stored.
The significant part of the checkpoint file name.
When set to "true", old checkpoint files will not be kept
The format of checkpoint files:
binary (3) or JSON (4)
A threshold beyond which optimization is expected to stop
Note that in order to activate this threshold, you also need to
set "hasQualityThreshold" to 1.
Activates (1) or de-activates (0) the quality threshold
The maximum allowed time-frame for the optimization
in the format hours:minutes:seconds
The minimum required time-frame for the optimization
in the format hours:minutes:seconds
Triggers emission (1) or omission (0) of information about reasons for termination
The likelihood for parent individuals to be "fused" together
rather than "just" being created through duplication schemes
The total size of the population
The number of parents in the population
The recombination method. Options
0: default
1: random selection from available parents
2: selection according to the parent's value
Specifies the number of individuals added per iteration
Specifies the maximum amount of individuals in the population
if growth is enabled
The sorting scheme. Options
0: MUPLUSNU mode with a single evaluation criterion
1: MUCOMMANU mode with a single evaluation criterion
2: MUCOMMANU mode with single evaluation criterion,
the best parent of the last iteration is retained
unless a better individual has been found
3: MUPLUSNU mode for multiple evaluation criteria, pareto selection
4: MUCOMMANU mode for multiple evaluation criteria, pareto selection
The step-size control strategy. Options
0: SELF_ADAPT (classic mutative sigma self-adaption, the legacy "ea")
1: SELF_ADAPT_SCALED (dimension-scaled tau = c/sqrt(2n)) [default]
2: ONE_FIFTH (Rechenberg 1/5 success rule on a single global sigma)
3: CSA (cumulative step-size adaptation on a single global sigma)
The learning-rate constant c used by SELF_ADAPT_SCALED (tau = c/sqrt(2n))
Whether to intermediate-recombine the per-individual sigma after recombination
